_about: What llm-launch gives opencode in its sessions: the plugins (with their options) and the opencode settings.
A new tested setup is an edit here plus a push; llm-launch offers the update at its next start on each machine.
setup_version: raise it when setup.sh gains a step every machine must run (a new llama.cpp build, say); opencode: the
version these plugins were tested with. After an update, the launcher offers to run setup.sh when either one moved on.
Plugin source: 'file' = a file in this repo, or 'url' + 'sha256' = downloaded once into ~/.config/llm-launch/plugins/
(kept only if the checksum matches). In option values, {kit} is this folder and {state} is ~/.config/llm-launch.
A replacement system prompt is a plugin too: a prompt file in prompts/, passed to its plugin as an option. A changed
prompt text gets a new file name, so each session can be matched to the tested setup it ran.
Only one plugin may replace opencode's own prompt: moving to a system-prompt plugin means removing the slim entry
(and tools.skill: false with it, if the tested setup kept the skill tool).
Before pushing a change here: python3 check-kit.py --fetch

plugins.name: compaction-anchor (slim part: short system prompt, shorter tool descriptions)
